contract_changes: All declared signatures are unchanged. Additive: ZFT.runs also exports MAX_ITEMS_PER_RUN (5000) and REPORTS_KEPT (20); the load.test API manifest still passes.

ZFT.runs.init(overrides) test seam is documented in runs.js: {state, items, config, progress, login, pdfCapture, net, browser, translators, zoteroOa, save, confirm, wasmHost ({get, shutdown}) or host, bodies (a store instance), createRunner, services, timers, clock, random}. Only the call that builds the controller uses them.

runs.startRun: mode defaults to 'full' and interactive defaults to false (the menu passes true explicitly). It also re-sends Configure in the same send as start_run when the prefs changed and no run is active, so a pane that forgot reconfigure() cannot leave stale settings. With runs active the change waits (pendingReconfigure) and is applied when the last run finishes. The controller keeps its own needConfigure flag (set at init and by onEngineFailure) and does not depend on how Runner.needsConfigure is maintained.

runs.shutdown: after the header steps it also calls state.dispose() as its last step, and resolves the done promise of any run the engine did not finish with a RunReport whose items are Outcome::Cancelled{by: shutdown} (so no caller waits forever). A concurrent init() during shutdown waits for it and then rebuilds.

runs only sends validated commands (u32 ids, known user-action kinds): one malformed command would make serde reject the whole StepIn and fail every run. Invalid cancelRun/cancelItem/userAction arguments are logged and dropped.

items.snapshot: lone surrogates in any string are replaced (serde_json rejects them); title is clipped by code point, not UTF-16 unit; library kinds other than group/feed (incl. 'publications') map to 'user'; an unknown library is reported files_editable:false. snapshot() throws if the attachment queries of a regular item fail, and snapshotAll turns that into a not-regular stub (skipped) instead of guessing 'no PDF'. snapshotAll drops entries that are not items (no integer id) with a log line. watchDeletions returns a no-op if observer registration fails.

state.js: the debounce timer is armed by the first unsaved change and is NOT pushed back by later ones, so a change reaches disk at most FLUSH_DEBOUNCE_MS (2000 ms) after it is made. sweepTmp keeps registrations for paths in opts.keep and for removals that failed (so the next sweep retries) rather than clearing the whole list, and counts only directories that actually existed. Malformed single ledger/halt/ezproxy/alma entries are dropped with a log instead of quarantining the whole file (serde would reject them on Configure); wrong top-level shapes still go to state.json.bad. set() ignores non-object values. registerTmpDir, nextRunId, getPersisted, dataDir and tmpRoot throw before init(); set, flush, reset, unregisterTmpDir and sweepTmp are quiet no-ops before init or after dispose.

contract_changes: All changes are additive; every name in tests/js/helpers/api-manifest.mjs is still exported.
net.js: RESPONSE_HEADERS gains 'akamai-grn', which the core classifier needs.

net.js: the file sink's JS backstop is an inactivity timer, re-armed on every onProgress (timeout_ms + 2000 of silence). Zotero's download() only bounds connect time and inactivity, so a total-time backstop would kill healthy 100 MB downloads. The memory sink keeps a total backstop of timeout_ms + 2000.
net.js: with successCodes:false, Zotero resolves a transport failure with xhr.status 0. net.js turns that into OpError tls or network and never returns it as a response.
pdf-capture.js: Capture gains pdfUrl() (the PDF's channel name), which browser.js uses as final_url when a PDF was captured.

pdf-capture.js: a second PDF in an already-satisfied capture is swallowed (onContent returns true). Only unknown browsers get false. capture() can throw OpError 'unsupported' (no MIMETypeHandler) or 'internal' (bad browser, or one that already has a capture).

browser.js: about:neterror, about:blocked and about:certerror end the load as OpError network, network and tls. The browser module's ordering is: PDF captured, error page, URL stable and not held, timeout.

zotero-oa.js: LOOKUP_BACKSTOP_MS is a new export (LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS + 7000). The completion is [{url, page_url, version}]. The frozen proto.rs ZoteroOaHit has a required url: String, so an entry with only a pageURL is emitted with url: "", never null or missing.

save.js: isStorableUrl refuses every host equal to or under the configured EZproxy suffix, a superset of the spec's first-label-contains-'-' rule. Reason: the login host and plain name.<suffix> hosts are proxy-internal too. It reads ZFT.config.getPref('institution.ezproxy_suffix').

save.js: after a successful save, or after cleanup on failure, the staged body record from ctx.bodies.get(handle) is mutated: consumed = true, dir = null, path = null. BodyStore.release must tolerate dir === null (no IO for it). get() must return the live record, not a copy, for this to take effect.
save.js: every save failure removes the staged temp dir, including validation failures such as already_has_pdf. The scope is checked up to the last validation; after that the save is not cancellable.
save.js: trim_prefix is verified to point at '%PDF-' after trimming. If not, it fails 'internal' and no attachment is created. Files over 512 MiB fail 'io'.

translators.js: the page is decoded through a Blob type with a charset. The charset comes from the contentType argument, else a <meta charset> sniff of the first 2 KiB, else utf-8. Without Zotero.Utilities.Internal.blobToHTMLDocument, a DOMParser + Zotero.HTTP.wrapDocument fallback is used. parsePage(bytes, url, contentType) is unchanged. The body is retained for the whole run, and release is awaited in a finally.
No new FTL ids. attachFile uses Zotero's own 'pane.item.attachments.select' string.

contract_changes: ADDITIVE, bodies.js: BodyStore.stageFile(path, len?) stages a streamed file that is not in the store yet (reads only head 4096 + tail 2048 via IOUtils.read offset/maxBytes; stats the file when len is missing); BodyStore.discardSlot(slot) removes and unregisters a slot that never became a body. allocPdfSlot returns exactly {dir, path}. Freeing tolerates info.dir === null (save.js marks a consumed body that way). deps also accepts attachments and pathUtils.

ADDITIVE, wasm-host.js: WasmInstance.reset() (guarded fx_reset), .abi/.generation/.traps fields; Host opts: timers {setTimeout, clearTimeout}, workerFactory(), workerUrl, url (also the wasm URL sent to the worker), and load() opt fetch(url). Worker-recycling policy: a worker that is recycled twice in a row without ever sending 'ready' (or cannot be created) switches the host to the main thread for good; a worker that never became ready is not charged an attempt against the request it held.

ADDITIVE, effects.js: Runner.reset() clears the failed flag; opts.disposeWaitMs (default 3000) bounds dispose(). While runner.failed is set, send() ignores every command EXCEPT 'configure', and a 'configure' command clears the flag and needsConfigure (this is how ZFT.runs resumes after onEngineFailure: it sends [configure, start_run]). pump() is inert while failed.

SEMANTICS the engine/js-ui/js-runs authors should know: login_window ops are parented on the RUN scope (cancel_item of the item that opened the shared window does not close it; cancel_run / Cancel{op} do). login_update: the fresh op is completed at once with ok {}, and login.update(windowOp, waiting) is called with the id(s) of the currently open login_window op(s); if the id given IS a live window op it is not completed. save_pdf: once the handler has started its scope is detached; engine Cancel{op}, cancel_item, cancel_run and run_finished do not cancel it (only engine failure or dispose do). Every op is answered exactly once: a JS-initiated cancel answers err.kind 'cancelled' immediately and the handler's late result (and any body it made) is dropped and released. Bodies carried by a completion the engine lists in StepOut.ignored are released by the runner. Stall check interval is stallMs/3: two consecutive stalled checks send DumpState once, the third fails the run(s) with Error('engine stalled'). run_finished cancels what is left of the run's scope (windows, hidden browsers) and forgets the run.

pdf::verdict: len = max(resp.body_len, staged length). If head_len is >= the body, the head is the whole body and its last 1024 bytes serve as the tail. Unsplit bodies search %%EOF in the last 1024 bytes only.

contract_changes: proto.rs, error.rs, lib.rs and Cargo.toml are unchanged. proto.rs is still the verbatim copy of the contract, with no additive changes.

Executor: spawn, run, cancel_where and wake_all are implemented as the spec describes. New `Executor::sweep_pending()` and `ReadyQueue::sweep_pending()`. `RunStats.more` is also true while a wake_all sweep has not yet been applied.

Reactor/ops: new `Reactor::drop_op(op) -> Dropped { Waiting | Completed(Vec<u32>) | Unknown }`. `Reactor::cancel` keeps its signature and now wraps it. `OpFuture::drop` on a slot that is already Done but never polled (item cancelled in the step that delivered the answer) now pushes `Release` for every body handle (`body`, `pdf`, `page`) in the payload, so JS handles are no longer leaked. Previously it pushed nothing.
Typed op wrappers: `Cx::decode` is now a method. A payload that cannot be decoded still becomes `OpErrKind::Internal`, and it now also emits `Release` for the body handles it carried.

`Timeout` drops the losing inner future when the timer wins, not when the Timeout value is dropped. `Cancel` is therefore emitted in the same poll that returns TimedOut, and polling again keeps answering TimedOut.

Engine::step follows the 9 phases. `not_configured` applies to StartRun only. CancelRun, CancelItem, UserAction, DumpState and Shutdown are accepted before Configure, because they ignore unknown runs. The stall sweep round gets its own POLL_BUDGET. `Stats.lost_wakes` is cumulative on `Engine`. The reentry error is sticky for the life of the engine. When the task table is full, a SpawnReq is dropped and an Error-level `Log` effect starting with 'executor full' is emitted.

sim: new `SimHost::{answer(op, Reply), pending_where(matcher), finish()}`, new public fields `ignored` and `steps`, and `sim::effect_op`. `Reply` and `Responder` keep their signatures. LoginUpdate completions are scheduled at the current time and are not registered in `pending`. Invariant failures return `EngineError { code: "invariant", .. }` (const `INVARIANT_CODE`). `run_until_idle` returns `sim_livelock` after 50,000 steps. `SimHost::finish()` runs `Invariant::finish` and run-sim's `run_scenario` should call it at the end.

contract_changes: Published signatures are unchanged. Additions are all inside owned files: oa::license_slug and oa::is_browser_walled (both pub), plus private oa/util.rs and oa/xml.rs. Nothing was added to model.rs.

rank::rank is a pure function of the SET of candidates. The final tie-break is URL, then source, not arrival order. This is deliberate: the spec's 'original index' tie-break would contradict its own shuffled-input test, and arrival order depends on which concurrent API call finishes first. rank(rank(x)) == rank(x) holds.

rank::rank also merges arXiv versions of one id (/pdf/X, /pdf/XvN, /abs/X) into the unversioned /pdf/X. It rewrites legacy PMC URLs but keeps any path after the id (.../PMC1/pdf/a.pdf stays a PDF path). rank::merge does not rewrite or drop anything, it only merges by canonical_key.

Found means at least one candidate. Two exceptions: the NCBI ID converter (Found when it learned an id) and bioRxiv pubs (Found when it carries published_doi:<doi> in note). A record that exists but offers nothing is Empty, with learned and oa_status still filled. Example: an OpenAlex closed work is Empty and still learns its PMID.

Notes are short fixed codes the engine can match on: published_doi:<doi> (bioRxiv), merged_record:<doi> (OpenAlex, when the work DOI differs from the request), bad_email (Unpaywall 422), no_pdf, not_held, unverified (CORE discover), doi_mismatch, no_match, no_results, not_in_pmc, no_such_key, plus http_<status> from gate. Notes never echo a body.

learned.doi is only offered when the request had no DOI (OpenAlex, Europe PMC, PMC, Crossref, Unpaywall, S2, CORE). OpenAlex also learns arxiv, pmid and pmcid from the PMC, PubMed and arXiv locations' own ids, as long as the request lacks them.

A list answer (OpenAlex results[], Europe PMC, ID converter) with several records and none matching the request returns Empty (no_match), not 'the first'. The spec said 'else the first'. I kept 'first' only when the request names no DOI, PMID or PMCID, and 'the only result' when the list has one entry.

Alma candidates use signal alma:<package_public_name>. CORE discover unwraps the redirect (fullTextLink?url=) to the https://core.ac.uk/reader/<id> landing page and drops the redirect key. Semantic Scholar's openAccessPdf.url is a Landing when it is not a file URL (the PLOS case returns doi.org).

oa::host_kind is a heuristic. It uses curated lists of publisher, aggregator and repository hosts, plus an academic-domain rule (.ac.uk, .edu, .ac.*) for Repository. Unknown hosts are Other and tier as DIRECT_REPOSITORY. The lists are not exhaustive; extend them in oa/mod.rs if hosts are misranked.

I could not check Alma against a real CTO response (the research doc only describes the shape). The parser accepts resolution_url as an element or as a key and falls back to a generic signal if package_public_name is missing; the hand-made tests/data/oa/alma-*.xml follow research/04 section 4.5.

Pre-existing, not mine: ids::clean_doi stops at '<' and '>', so SICI-style DOIs containing them are truncated. I kept that behaviour as the spec asked. I added control characters as DOI terminators and made trim_trailing linear-time without changing its results.

contract_changes: ABI v1 is unchanged: the seven pinned exports and the additive fx_login_state keep their signatures. One test-only export, fx_debug_panic(code: u32) -> u32, exists behind the new cargo feature `debug-panic` (off by default). `cargo xtask build` now verifies the wasm and fails the command on a violation: it must have no imports, exactly the 11 documented exports, no builder path fragments, and be at most 700 KiB raw (it warns above 450 KiB). It verifies before staging, so a bad module is never copied into plugin/. The staging copy is atomic (temp file plus rename).
`cargo xtask test` and `check` run the Node tests as `node --test "tests/js/*.test.mjs"` with ZFT_DEBUG_WASM set, because Node 24 rejects a bare directory. `test` builds the debug-panic module first.

The `harness` command creates a fresh run root under <target>/xtask/harness/ (with a unique name) and passes it to run.ps1 as -RunsRoot, with -RunName run.

Deliberate refinements of the written classifier rules, documented in the classify.rs module docs. (1) A Cloudflare challenge or block is also recognised when the server header is ABSENT and the body has Cloudflare-only markers, because the OA-side fixtures carry only a content-type; a different server value still rules Cloudflare out. ADDED on Cx (acquire.rs): disable_api(src) and disable_api_for(src, ms) switch an OA API off (refuses with HostSkipped); block_host(key, for_ms) persists a block on a publisher family or OA host; wall_host(host, reason) walls an OA host for 30 min at once (F7 hard block, which had no entry point); host_skipped(host).

BEHAVIOUR: Permit::report(ok) now also drives two breakers. 5 failures in a row wall an OA host for 30 min (policy::HOST_WALL_TTL_MS); 3 in a row switch an OA API off for 5 min. acquire_oa_host, note_challenge and HostBook normalise host keys (lower-case, one leading www. dropped). HostBook::note_outcome_at, note_challenge_at, is_skipped_at and wall_at carry the monotonic clock. The old clock-less methods stay and never expire.

BEHAVIOUR: Limiter::release applies max(gap_ms, spec.min_gap_ms), so InstHost (2 s) and OaHost (1 s) specs carry their gap. A grant wakes the new head. Limiter gained check/take/park/set_spec/all_wakers; poll/release/forget/waiting keep their signatures.

BEHAVIOUR: Ledger::commit stamps the entry with the reservation's wall time (capped at the commit wall), not the commit time, so no window can ever exceed its cap. The estimate of one reservation is clamped to the MB/hour cap. A cap of 0 is an immediate hit with reset_at = wall + 24 h. When several caps bind, the hit names the one that frees last (ties: hourly, daily, MB/hour).
BEHAVIOUR: AcquireInst joins the global queue only once its own family gate would grant, so items waiting out a family gap never block other families.

ADDED on Sched: refusal(), inst_gap_ms(), begin_shutdown(), is_shutting_down(), gate_wakers(), inst_wakers(), halts_effect(), dump(wall). Added policy items PROBE_STALE_MS, LOGIN_ENGINE_GRACE_MS, API_FAIL_LIMIT, API_COOLDOWN_MS, HOST_WALL_TTL_MS, clamp_item_concurrency(), pdf_gap_ms().

ADDED on login.rs: LoginGate.shutdown field and LoginGate::dump(); InteractiveGate keeps held_by and queue and gains a private next_ticket plus enqueue/try_take/release; RealmState keeps its pub(crate) fields and gains private ones. waiting_user() now counts parked session_admit callers too, so the stall detector stays quiet while the engine waits on a probe or a SignInNow.

BEHAVIOUR: on_shutdown also marks the scheduler as shutting down (later acquire and reserve calls resolve ShuttingDown) and wakes challenge windows queued on the gate. session_admit checks realm-wide Refused/Halted first, then lets a working session (SignedIn) serve every run, and only then applies a run's block. The prompt cap (MAX_PROMPTS_PER_REALM) limits opening windows per run; joining an open window is always allowed. A decline or timeout is tagged on every run with a parked caller (login and admit). A dropped window driver cleans up the realm (DriverGuard) and tags the waiting runs TimedOut. The engine-side login timer is login_timeout_sec plus a 5 s grace, so JS's own Timeout result normally wins.

[from engine] JS EFFECT RUNNER, protocol interpretations that docs/design/plugin-js.md already matches: (1) `barrier: true` on Http/BrowserLoad means a persist barrier: await earlier `Persist{flush:true}` writes first; the engine pushes the ledger Persist BEFORE the barrier fetch in the same StepOut. (2) `Release{handle}` is idempotent and is emitted for every BodyRef the engine received, including after SavePdf completes; bodies in completions listed in `StepOut.ignored` must be released by JS. (3) `LoginUpdate.op` is a FRESH op id, never the LoginWindow's id; JS completes it immediately and it lands in `ignored`. Completing the window's op id instead would end the window early. (4) `Cancel{op}` on a LoginWindow closes the window; on SavePdf it is ignored if the save has started (saving items are not cancelled). (5) `ZoteroOa` completion is a JSON array of ZoteroOaHit. (6) `Configure` may be re-sent; `persisted` is applied only by the first one per instance. (7) `retain` is Page for landing pages, Pdf for PDF fetches, None otherwise. (8) Effect order inside a StepOut is meaningful.
